research_record.findings: Groth Music identifies a piano score and separate solo alto part, dedicated to Lawrence Gwozdz. The four movements are Monhegan Island, Christmas Cove, Boothbay Harbor, and Cadillac Mountain. Both the opening score and separate alto part carry the composer date 1991. research_record.score_observations: Inspected seven public notation images: the opening piano score, score pages 12, 13, 18, 28, and 29, and the first separate alto-part page. This is a sample across all four movements, not the complete sonata. The piano-score solo line is in concert pitch, sometimes using bass clef; the separate alto part is transposed for E-flat saxophone. At the opening the score has three flats while the alto part has no key-signature accidentals. Monhegan Island begins Andante, quarter note approximately 84, with long slurs, dotted figures, accidentals and broken-chord piano accompaniment. The separate alto-part page through approximately measure 29 includes quick ascending runs, triplet groups, chromatic notes, written pitches several ledger lines above the staff, and contrasting expressive/dynamic markings. These visible high-register passages establish an upper-register demand without establishing the complete range. Christmas Cove begins Larghetto, quarter note approximately 66, with a piano introduction, legato solo phrasing and triplet figures. Boothbay Harbor is a 6/8 scherzo, Allegro grazioso, with a tempo marking of 116–120, with staccato eighth-note patterns and chromatic motion. Cadillac Mountain opens slowly with intensity, ad libitum quasi cadenza, then shows Largo quarter note 56, irregular subdivisions, fermatas, chromatic lines and changing meter on page 29.

Its manuscript heading gives Worley’s date 1962; the printed footer gives a separate 2001 Elkan-Vogel copyright. The 1962 date is therefore supported directly by the score rather than inferred from publication. Groth’s exact listing gives Moderato, Adagio, and Molto Allegro. The orchestral recording calls the first movement Allegro moderato. These movement labels come from their respective sources and should not be silently normalized. Professional performance is documented by Albany’s recording with Lawrence Gwozdz, alto saxophone, the Bohuslav Martinu Philharmonic and conductor Kirk Trevor. Juan Daniel Oviedo-Reina’s own video description documents movement III with Darío Martin, piano, at a Fall 2020 saxophone studio jury in the University of Southern Mississippi School of Music. The saxophone staff is labeled E-flat alto saxophone and is transposed; its key signature differs from the piano. This is only the first movement’s opening, not a complete solo-part inspection. The opening is Moderato, quarter note 112–120, initially in common time. After orchestral material in the piano and several solo rests, the saxophone enters at mf. The visible solo then moves into 5/4 with slurred beamed groups, staccato notes, accidentals, a crescendo, and a leap to a pitch several ledger lines above the staff. A change to common time and later return to 5/4 are visible. The piano reduction includes chromatic chords, sustained bass notes, accented repeated chords and beamed runs.
